en: Only a member turns watching on or off, and this came from an automated credential. Nothing was changed.
Say whether this document is watched, yes or no, and, if you give one, how often, as one of the listed frequencies ({field} isn't). Nothing was changed.

en: That isn't a value this setting takes. Choose one of the setting's own values. Nothing was changed.
That value can't be kept as a setting: a setting holds words, numbers, yes or no, or a list of those. Nothing was changed.

en: That handle and password don't match. Check both and try again; after several tries, sign-in pauses for a while to keep others from guessing.
note: credentials R4; never says which handles exist

en: Sign-in is paused for a while after too many tries from here. This keeps others from guessing passwords; it isn't a judgement on you. Try again at {time}.
note: credentials R38; {time} the local time the pause ends

en: That didn't work: the handle, the code or both aren't right, or the code was already used. Check them and try again. Nothing was changed.
note: credentials R47; one answer for every arm

en: You aren't signed in here any more: your sign-in ended, or you signed out on another device. Sign in again to go back to where you were.
A password needs at least 12 characters. A short sentence you can remember works well. Nothing was changed.
Your current password isn't right, so it wasn't changed. Check it and try again.
Your group's Civicsmith already has its first administrator, so this one-time password no longer works. If that was you, sign in instead.
This invitation link doesn't work: it may have been used, passed its seven days, or been withdrawn. Ask whoever sent it for a new one.
This join link doesn't work: it may have been replaced or turned off. Ask the group for its current link.
note: membership R104; one answer for each arm

en: The group's join link has let in as many people as it allows today. Try again tomorrow.
Say the name the group will know you by. Only its administrators see it. Nothing was changed.
You are signed out on this device. Your work is saved in your group's Civicsmith, not here.
note: the front door after signing out

en: You were signed out after a while away, so nobody else at this device can use your sign-in. Sign in again to go back to the page you were on.
note: D3 (K3061): 15 minutes idle on a shared device; 12 hours on one kept signed in

en: Locked after 30 minutes away. Enter your password to go on where you were; nothing was lost.
note: D3 (K3061): a device kept signed in

en: For this, enter your password again: signing or publishing a case, changing administrators and connecting Claude always ask.
My own: keep me signed in (it locks after 30 minutes away; you sign in again after 12 hours)
Shared or public: sign me out after 15 minutes away
Did you set this group up? Your handle is admin.

You sign as {signer}, an owner of {project}. The public page will read “Published by {group} · signed by {signer}”. Once public, anyone can read it and check your signature without asking the group; it can be corrected by a new edition, never removed.
Your device is asking you to confirm with your signing key: its own window asks for your passphrase, fingerprint or device PIN. The key never leaves this device, and Civicsmith never sees it.
Your device didn't confirm, so nothing was signed or published. Everything is as it was; sign again when you are ready.
Signed. Edition {edition} becomes public on {date} at {time} ({zone}). Until then it waits, not public. At that time Civicsmith checks again and publishes only if nothing changed since you signed.
Signed and published. Edition {edition} is public now: anyone can read it and check your signature without the group.
You have no signing key in this browser. Register one here: it is made on this device and never leaves it, and every use asks you to confirm. Then you come back to this step, with nothing lost.
Keep this key on this device, so you can sign here again without loading it. Leave this unticked on a computer others use: you then load your key file each time you sign.
note: K3079: kept only when the member chooses

en: Only an owner of {project} signs its cases: {owners}. Everything you prepared stays as it is. Ask one of them to sign.
Signing and publishing finish on a larger screen. Everything here can be read on a phone. Open {project} on a computer to sign: the ceremony is where you left it.
